cards.q: Pregnancy test kits: antibody target and what they detect
cards.a: Antibodies to the unique subunit of hCG; qualitative detection within a few days of a missed period

cards.q: Quantitative plasma hCG: method and uses
cards.a: Radioimmunoassay; checks normal pregnancy progress, ectopic pregnancy, mole, choriocarcinoma

cards.q: Thyroid function assays: methods (GG12)
cards.a: Radioimmunoassays, then chemiluminescent and enzyme-linked immunoassays for T4, T3 and TSH

cards.q: Free T4 gold-standard method and its limit
cards.a: Equilibrium dialysis with radioimmunoassay of the dialysate; costly, rarely in routine labs

cards.q: Routine free T4 and T3 assays: principle
cards.a: Labelled iodothyronine analogues in chemiluminescent or enzyme-linked assays; affected by binding proteins and illness

cards.q: Serum TSH: role in thyroid testing with normal pituitary
cards.a: Thyroid function test of choice

cards.q: Digoxin levels: method
cards.a: Radioimmunoassay of serum digoxin

cards.q: Digoxin: concentration range with therapeutic efficacy
Digoxin: concentration linked to increased mortality
cards.a: Above 1.2 ng/mL

cards.q: Urine toxicology screen: how fast it gives results
cards.a: Immunoassay; turnaround about 1 hour

cards.q: Drugs of abuse detected by urine immunoassay screens: list
cards.a: Amphetamines, barbiturates, benzodiazepines, cannabis, cocaine, opiates

cards.q: Limits of urine immunoassay screens
cards.a: False positives from cross-reactivity; long detection windows can mislead about acute toxicity

cards.q: Pharmacokinetics became possible in the 20th century because of
cards.a: Sensitive methods such as high-performance chromatography and mass spectrometry

cards.q: Peptide purification and synthesis advance from the 1970s
cards.a: High-performance liquid chromatography with solid-phase peptide synthesis

cards.q: Metabolomics platforms: list
cards.a: 1H-NMR; liquid or gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry, with chemometric and multivariate analysis

cards.q: Metabolomics: definition
cards.a: Systematic identification and quantification of all metabolites in a sample

cards.q: Metabolomics output in drug development
cards.a: Simultaneous measurement of thousands of chemicals in serum, urine, cells or tissues

cards.q: Metabolites in urine identified by
cards.a: Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry

cards.q: Drugs with low safety margin where TDM is useful: list
cards.a: Digoxin, anticonvulsants, antiarrhythmics, theophylline, aminoglycosides, lithium, tricyclic antidepressants

cards.q: TDM is particularly useful in these situations: list
cards.a: Low safety margin; large individual variation; toxic drug with renal failure; poisoning; unexplained failure; compliance checks

cards.q: TDM for long-acting drugs: sample timing for dose adjustment
cards.a: Trough steady-state level, just before the next dose

cards.q: TDM for short-acting drugs (e.g. ampicillin, gentamicin): sample timing
cards.a: Immediate post-absorptive phase, about 1-2 h after oral or i.m. dose, to reflect peak

cards.q: Blood level in poisoning: when to sample and why repeat
cards.a: Earliest sample to confirm poisoning; repeat to estimate clearance and need to hasten elimination (e.g. haemodialysis)

cards.q: Random drug level sampling: use
cards.a: Informative for checking compliance

cards.q: Drugs where plasma level monitoring is of no value: list
cards.a: Antihypertensives, hypoglycaemics, diuretics, oral anticoagulants, inhalational anaesthetics (response measurable); levodopa (activated in body); reserpine, guanethidine, MAO inhibitors, omeprazole (hit and run); organophosphates, phenoxybenzamine (irreversible)

cards.q: Doping detection: androgen other than testosterone
cards.a: Gas chromatography and mass spectrometry, if still taken at testing

cards.q: Exogenous testosterone: first detection method
cards.a: T/E ratio: urinary testosterone glucuronide to epitestosterone glucuronide

cards.q: Why the T/E ratio rises with exogenous testosterone
cards.a: Exogenous testosterone suppresses epitestosterone, so only testosterone is raised

cards.q: Exogenous testosterone: second detection method
cards.a: Gas chromatography-combustion-isotope ratio mass spectrometry of 13C/12C in urinary steroids

cards.q: Isotope ratio result: what a low 13C/12C ratio means
cards.a: Steroid probably from a pharmaceutical source, not endogenous

cards.q: Doping with newer designer androgen: why hard to detect
cards.a: Tetrahydrogestrinone (THG) designed to avoid antidoping detection by structure and rapid catabolism

cards.q: Principle of colorimetry
cards.a: Colour intensity tracks concentration; read from light absorbed at the right wavelength

cards.q: Langendorff cardiac glycoside test: potassium measured by
cards.a: Flame photometry of the coronary outflow

cards.q: Langendorff glycoside test: rise in potassium outflow indicates
cards.a: Positive inotropic effect (correlates well)

cards.q: General ELISA steps in order: list all
cards.a: Coat wells with antigen; block unbound sites; add primary antibody; add enzyme-linked secondary antibody; add substrate forming coloured product

cards.q: Purpose of the blocking step in ELISA
cards.a: Blocks unbound sites to prevent false positives

cards.q: HRP and TMB ELISA: colour after acid and wavelength read
cards.a: Yellow; read at 450 nm

cards.q: Fluorescence polarisation immunoassay (FPIA): principle
cards.a: Fluorescein-labelled drug competes with patient's drug for antibody; more drug means less polarised light

cards.q: Thin-layer chromatography: use and limitation
cards.a: Cheap, quick qualitative purity checks (e.g. alkaloids); only semi-quantitative

cards.q: Toxin analysis methods used qualitatively
cards.a: Colorimetric and UV-visible spectrophotometry

cards.q: Toxin analysis methods used quantitatively: list all
cards.a: Infrared spectroscopy, gas chromatography, HPLC, immunoassay

cards.q: Why radioimmunoassay is now rarely used in clinical labs
cards.a: Radioisotope safety needs; ELISA replaces the radioisotope with an enzyme

cards.q: Flame photometry: emitting species in the flame
cards.a: Excited atoms falling back to a lower energy state

cards.q: Flame photometry: wavelength identifies
cards.a: The element (each has its own emission spectrum)

cards.q: Flame photometer: detector
cards.a: Detector; output proportional to concentration

cards.q: Flame photometry: how concentration is found
cards.a: Read standards of known strength, compare unknown

cards.q: Clinical analytes measured by flame photometry
cards.a: Sodium and potassium

cards.q: Radioimmunoassay: nature of the assay
cards.a: Physico-chemical test-tube assay (not a bioassay)

cards.q: Radioimmunoassay: what labelled and unlabelled hormone compete for
cards.a: Limited binding sites of a specific antibody

cards.q: Ratio plotted on the radioimmunoassay standard curve
cards.a: Bound to free (B/F) ratio of labelled hormone, against standard concentration

cards.q: Trend of B/F ratio as unlabelled hormone rises
cards.a: Falls progressively

cards.q: How the unknown plasma level is found in radioimmunoassay
cards.a: Read the B/F ratio off the standard curve run under identical conditions

cards.q: Antibody type from repeated immunisation of animals
cards.a: Polyclonal (monoclonal from hybridoma gives superior assays)

cards.q: Radioisotope used to label the hormone in radioimmunoassay
cards.a: Radioiodine

cards.q: Retention factor (Rf) in TLC: formula
cards.a: Distance moved by compound / distance moved by solvent

cards.q: TLC: nature of the technique and main limitation
cards.a: Cheap, rapid, semi-quantitative; mainly qualitative

cards.q: HPLC compared with column chromatography
cards.a: Solvent forced through at up to about 400 atmospheres, not gravity; faster, finer particles

cards.q: Normal-phase HPLC: column and solvent
cards.a: Polar silica; non-polar solvent such as hexane

cards.q: Reversed-phase HPLC: column and solvent
cards.a: Silica with long hydrocarbon chains; polar solvent such as water-methanol

cards.q: Most commonly used form of HPLC
cards.a: Reversed phase

cards.q: Normal-phase HPLC: compounds that emerge first
cards.a: Non-polar compounds

cards.q: Reversed-phase HPLC: compounds that emerge first
cards.a: Polar compounds

cards.q: HPLC retention time: definition
cards.a: Time from injection to maximum peak height of the compound

cards.q: Factors that change HPLC retention time: list all
cards.a: Pressure, stationary phase (material and particle size), solvent composition, column temperature

cards.q: HPLC peak area is proportional to
cards.a: Amount of compound passing the detector

cards.q: Common HPLC detector principle
cards.a: UV absorption of eluate

cards.q: HPLC coupled to mass spectrometer: advantage
cards.a: Compounds identified from fragmentation pattern without known retention times

cards.q: Preparative HPLC: purpose
cards.a: Isolation and purification of compounds

cards.q: Mass spectrometry: what it measures
cards.a: Mass-to-charge ratio and abundance of gas-phase ions

cards.q: Main components of a mass spectrometer: list
cards.a: Ion source, analyser, detector

cards.q: Ionisation techniques in mass spectrometry: list all
cards.a: Electron impact, chemical ionisation, fast atom bombardment, field ionisation, plasma desorption

cards.q: Hyphenated mass spectrometry techniques: list all
cards.a: GC-MS, LC-MS, HPLC-MS

cards.q: Mass spectrum is a plot of
cards.a: Ion abundance against mass-to-charge ratio

cards.q: Radioimmunoassay: sensitivity limit
cards.a: Picogram amounts with high-affinity antibody

cards.q: Drugs and substances measured by RIA: list
cards.a: Hormones, digoxin or digitoxin, morphine, amphetamine

cards.q: RIA: hazard of radioiodine in the body
cards.a: Concentrates in the thyroid if accidentally taken

cards.q: Disadvantages of RIA: list all
cards.a: Costly short-lived label, gamma counter needed, radiation hazard, licence and disposal, narrow range, hard to automate

cards.q: RIA: type of analysis
cards.a: Indirect, saturation analysis (reagent less than analyte)

cards.q: PSA measured by RIA: diagnostic use
cards.a: Prostate cancer

cards.q: FPIA: free tracer versus antibody-bound tracer polarisation
cards.a: Free tracer: low polarisation; bound tracer: higher (slower rotation)

cards.q: FPIA: effect of more drug in sample on polarisation
cards.a: Lower polarisation (less labelled drug bound to antibody)

cards.q: Drugs of abuse detectable by FPIA: list all
cards.a: Cannabinoids, amphetamines, barbiturates, cocaine, benzodiazepines, methadone, opiates, PCP

cards.q: FPIA: advantages and main disadvantage
cards.a: Fast, sensitive, easy; serum background interference needs blank

cards.q: ELISA types: list all
cards.a: Direct, indirect, sandwich, competitive

cards.q: ELISA type with highest sensitivity from secondary-antibody amplification
cards.a: Indirect ELISA

cards.q: Competitive ELISA: higher sample antigen gives
cards.a: Weaker signal

cards.q: Steady-state level versus predicted value
cards.a: May be 1/3 to 3 times the predicted

cards.q: Revised dose rate formula in TDM (first-order)
cards.a: Previous rate x target level / measured steady-state level

cards.q: TDM sample time in poisoning
cards.a: As early as possible, then repeat

cards.q: T/E ratio: full name
cards.a: Urinary testosterone glucuronide to epitestosterone glucuronide ratio

cards.q: Recombinant hormone misused for blood doping
cards.a: Recombinant erythropoietin (epoetin alfa)

cards.q: Why epoetin misuse by athletes is discouraged
cards.a: Implicated in deaths of several athletes

cards.q: Technique that distinguishes pharmaceutical from endogenous testosterone
cards.a: Isotope-ratio mass spectrometry (13C/12C)

cards.q: Colorimetry: light range measured
cards.a: Visible range only

cards.q: Colorimetry: filter colour relative to absorbing substance
cards.a: Complementary colour

cards.q: Beer-Lambert law: absorbance is directly proportional to
cards.a: Concentration of the absorbing chemical (at fixed wavelength and path length)

cards.q: Physical half-life of 131I
cards.a: About 8 days

cards.q: 131I emission used for tracing
cards.a: Gamma rays

cards.q: 131I emission that destroys thyroid cells
cards.a: Beta particles

cards.q: Stable (non-radioactive) iodine isotope
Route of therapeutic 131I
cards.a: Oral sodium salt of 131I in water

cards.q: Commonest indication for radioactive iodine therapy
cards.a: Hyperthyroidism

cards.q: Diagnostic 131I dose range
cards.a: 25-100 microcurie

cards.q: Radioisotope favoured for linking to monoclonal antibody
cards.a: 131I (readily available, inexpensive)

cards.q: Enzyme that drives PCR
cards.a: DNA polymerase

cards.q: Three steps of one PCR cycle
cards.a: Denaturation, annealing, extension

cards.q: Inventor of PCR and year
cards.a: Kary Mullis, 1984

cards.q: Year PCR won the Nobel Prize
cards.a: 1993 (Chemistry)

cards.q: Gene used for bacterial identification in metagenomics
cards.a: 16S rRNA

cards.q: Gel and stain used to view separated DNA fragments
cards.a: Agarose gel with ethidium bromide

cards.q: Lowest concentration that stops visible growth after 18-24 h
cards.a: MIC (minimum inhibitory concentration)

cards.q: Dilution series used for MIC
cards.a: Doubling concentrations

cards.q: Disk diffusion clear area around disk
cards.a: Zone of inhibition

cards.q: Susceptibility rule against breakpoint
cards.a: MIC at or below the breakpoint = susceptible

cards.q: Adjusting sample strength against a standard
cards.a: Biostandardisation

cards.q: Large MBC-to-MIC difference means
cards.a: Bacteriostatic action

cards.q: Lag in regrowth after brief antibiotic exposure
cards.a: Post-antibiotic effect (PAE)

cards.q: Clinical use of MBC
cards.a: Not used to guide antibiotic selection

cards.q: Biomarker definition
cards.a: Objectively measured indicator of normal or pathogenic process, or drug response

cards.q: Surrogate marker function
cards.a: Substitutes for a clinical endpoint; predicts clinical benefit

cards.q: Example surrogate marker of clinical benefit
cards.a: Blood pressure

cards.q: Clinical endpoint: how a patient feels, functions or survives
cards.a: Clinical endpoint (outcome)

cards.q: Premarketing surrogate endpoints: examples
cards.a: Blood pressure, lipid levels, HbA1c, CD4 count

cards.q: Antiarrhythmics misleading surrogate
cards.a: Flecainide and encainide: fewer VPDs, more mortality after MI (CAST)

cards.q: Endogenous probes for OATP1B and OCT2/MATE
cards.a: Coproporphyrin-I (OATP1B); N-methylnicotinamide (OCT2/MATE)

cards.q: Genetic test before carbamazepine
cards.a: HLA-B*1502

cards.q: Genetic test before rasburicase
cards.a: G6PD deficiency

cards.q: Gene variants guiding warfarin dose
cards.a: VKORC1 (AA variant) with CYP2C9

cards.q: Melanoma biomarker for vemurafenib
cards.a: BRAF V600E mutation

cards.q: Biomarker for trastuzumab
cards.a: HER2/neu overexpression

cards.q: Biomarker for imatinib
cards.a: Philadelphia chromosome

cards.q: Validation criterion before a biomarker becomes surrogate
cards.a: Biological plausibility

cards.q: Entire set of metabolites within a cell
cards.a: Metabolome

cards.q: Quantitative protein expression profile of a cell, organism or tissue
cards.a: Proteome

cards.q: Two methods used to compare protein expression between tumour and normal tissue
cards.a: 2D gel electrophoresis and mass spectrometry

cards.q: Four conceptual approaches in metabolomics: list
cards.a: Target analysis, metabolite profiling, metabolomics, metabolic fingerprinting

cards.q: Two most widely used detection techniques in metabolomics
cards.a: NMR and mass spectrometry

cards.q: Metabolomics detection technique that needs no prior separation
cards.a: NMR spectroscopy (sample can be recovered)

cards.q: Four steps of a metabolomics experiment
cards.a: Sample collection and preparation; separation and detection; data mining and extraction; data analysis

cards.q: Body fluid where metabolomics fingerprints liver, kidney and CNS toxicity in animals
cards.a: Urine

cards.q: Omics layer: mRNA transcribed from thousands of genes at once
cards.a: Transcriptomics (transcriptome)

cards.q: Omics layer: thousands of translated proteins quantified together
cards.a: Proteomics

cards.q: Why proteomics is harder than genomics
cards.a: Protein expression changes with time and environment; the genome is nearly constant

cards.q: Metabolic profiling use in new drug development
cards.a: Toxicity assessment before clinical trials
